arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Christina Swarns argued for Buck. She stated his lawyers introduced a biased opinion. She claimed the opinion linked his race to violence. She asked the Court to excuse the deadline.
Mr. Keller argued for the state. He defended the death sentence. He cited the specific murders committed by Buck. He argued the deadline must be enforced.
Justice Alito called the trial conduct indefensible. He noted the unusual nature of the case. He questioned the how the case got here of the appeal.
Justice Sotomayor questioned the retroactivity of recent rulings. She asked how the argument applies to this case. She highlighted the circuit split on the issue.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Duane Buck faces the death penalty. His lawyers introduced a biased expert opinion. He missed the deadline to appeal that error. He asks the Court to excuse the missed deadline. The state says the deadline stands. The Court must decide if this excuse applies.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Buck wants the Court to excuse his missed deadline. He argues his lawyers failed him. He wants a new chance to appeal.
The state wants the Court to uphold the deadline. It argues Buck failed to act on time. It wants the death sentence to stand.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Buck argues his lawyers committed ineffective assistance. He claims this failure justifies excusing the deadline. He cites recent Supreme Court guidance on this issue.
The state argues the deadline is strict. It claims Buck cannot use this excuse. It says the lower courts applied the correct standard.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked if the Third Circuit test applies here. She questioned the retroactivity of recent rulings. She noted a split among the circuits.
Chief Justice Roberts asked about the tension in Buck's briefing. He noted the focus on the underlying merits. He questioned the scope of the rule being applied.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of procedural deadlines. It affects how courts handle missed appeals. It determines if ineffective counsel can excuse delays. The outcome shapes future death penalty appeals. It clarifies the balance between finality and fairness.
